name: porsche_carrera_gt_v10
label: Porsche Carrera GT 5.7 L V10 (68°, firing 68°/76°)
based_on: Porsche Carrera GT 5.7 L V10, type 980/01 (2003-2006)

sources.what: Porsche Newsroom article (28 Sep 2025) with a technical data table for the Carrera GT. Manufacturer.
Excellence magazine (Porsche specialist) spec table: bore, stroke, max rpm.
Autozine technical review of the Carrera GT; single-author enthusiast site, source of the 68/76 firing statement.
kfz-tech.de (German automotive engineering teaching site) note on the Carrera GT V10: shared crank pins with unequal intervals.
English Wikipedia Porsche V10 engine page; bore, stroke, redline.
German Wikipedia Carrera GT page; valvetrain description.
Supercar Nostalgia guide; noted only for its contradictory rod-material sentence.

notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, compression, 68-degree bank, two rods per crank pin, four valves per cylinder, 8400 rpm maximum, fixed-length intake with inlet funnels. The 68/76-degree firing alternation rests on a single enthusiast source (Autozine); no Porsche document stating it was found, though it is what a 68-degree bank with five shared pins 72 degrees apart must give. The firing ORDER and cylinder numbering were not found: the order used (1-6-5-10-2-7-3-8-4-9, cylinders 1-5 on one bank) is assumed. Estimated, not sourced: rod length, valve diameters and lifts, cam timing and duration (variable intake timing on the real engine; one fixed timing is used), a plenum intake with one throttle (the throttle arrangement was not found), runner sizes, exhaust layout (5-into-1 per bank, no cross-over) and all its sizes, idle speed. Left to the simulator's defaults: plenum, throttle and airbox, collector volume, muffler, flywheel inertia. Also estimates: friction_scale, heat_q, burn_scale (the simulator's friction, heat-release and burn-rate scales), set with the other estimated fields so that simulated torque and power come near the published figures; no sourced number was changed.
